text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Egypt will set off towards the next century with the help of education, information and decision making. President Hosni Mubarak tours information support centres, says the developments in the region do not require an Arab summit meeting. We are awaiting the results of the efforts being made to save the peace process. Government approves 12 billion pounds ($3.5 billion) for education in this year's budget.

- Foreign Minister Amr Moussa to sign five agreements with India in New Delhi. The two countries will cooperate in the fields of civil aviation and scientific research, prompting investment and tourism, and exchanging media programming.
- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri will discuss prompting economic cooperation with Germany's Economic Cooperation Minister Carl-Dieter Spranger.
- German minister Spranger says Mubarak's policies have given international respect to Egypt.
- Mubarak sends a letter to Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi.
- Moussa says Egypt is ready to mediate between Israel and the Palestinians to revive the peace process if Israel stops its settlement policies.
- Akhbar has learned that the finance ministry is considering reducing taxes on Egypt's employees.
- Mubarak says teachers are responsible to build generations capable of modernising Egypt.
- Ganzouri approves 28 new investment projects, including 12 in southern Egypt and six in new communities.
- New budget includes 52 billion pounds of tax revenues.
